newsitem.title: UK: NWE naphtha steady to firm amid low demand.
newsitem.headline: NWE naphtha steady to firm amid low demand.

text.p: NWE naphtha was steady to slightly firmer as relaxed end-user demand dampened the bullish influence of higher crude prices, traders said.
A pipeline spec cargo out of Grangemouth loading at the end of the week was believed to still be on offer.
Traders said the seller was offering the cargo around the $201-$202 a tonne cif NWE level.

Russian fob barrels were also reported to be on offer at quotes lo. "Petrochem buyers are looking for high paraffinic content material and the full range material isn't too much in demand," said one trader.
Traders said swaps had been talked at higher levels in early trade but were assessed at $207/$208 cif NWE for April later on.
"It doesn't matter how tight or how high crude is, if there's no demand there's no demand," one trader said.
Market players said a number of buyers had turned to alternative material such as LPG because they deemed current prices too high.
